chore(beads): file two ethos doc defects found reviewing the enable output

Copilot reviewed PR #220 and raised three findings against the files
`ethos enable` deposited. Two are real and are now items 6 and 7 on
xboing-pf7d; the third does not hold and was counter-argued.

VALID — .punt-labs/ethos/ETHOS-SETUP.md:39,:110 claims `ethos enable`
registers the SessionStart / PreCompact / pre-commit hooks in
.claude/settings.json. It does not. Measured: this repo's settings.json
declares PreCompact and SessionStart events with ZERO mentions of ethos —
they are beads' bd hooks. Enable's own output never mentions settings.json;
it reports vendored, gitignore, marker, import, hook:pre-commit chained,
hook:commit-msg installed. Ethos's session hooks come from the plugin, not
repo settings.

VALID — .beads/hooks/commit-msg's header says trailers are appended "when
env is set" and that it passthroughs "when neither env var is set". It does
not passthrough: it falls back to `ethos hook commit-trailers` to resolve
the committing session. The body documents that fallback explicitly, so the
header contradicts its own file. This one has bite — my earlier analysis on
xboing-yeuw had the wrong shape until I read the hook line by line, because
the header implies no-env means no-work when in fact it does the session
lookup that is precisely where the chain breaks.

NOT VALID — .beads/hooks/pre-commit:36. Copilot read "git starts the hook
with $? = 0" as a general claim. It is a parenthetical scoped by "when this
runs standalone", and the same sentence continues "or the host hook's
fall-through status when this is chained after a foreign hook". Lines 44-49
restate both branches. The comment is accurate and complete.

NEITHER VALID FINDING IS FIXED IN THE FILE, deliberately. Both live in
artifacts `ethos enable` deposits, and enable is idempotent by design —
"re-running is the upgrade path". A local edit is clobbered on the next run
and, worse, hides the defect from the generator that emits it. Same
principle applied to missions.jsonl earlier today: do not edit an artifact
to read correctly when the thing writing it is what is wrong.

xboing-pf7d now carries seven ethos items. Item 5 — session binding emitting
"no session in context" on every mission create — remains the root cause
behind xboing-yeuw part 2 and the reason the newly installed trailer hook
stamps nothing.

Also recorded there: removing a git worktree with an active ethos session
loses unsealed audit lines, and there is no warning at removal time — only
later at commit time, when it is too late to recover them.
EOF

tool_input.command:
cd ~/Coding/punt-labs/ethos && bd create --title="Session resolution keyed on an unstable Claude PID — trailers never stamp under the daemon/bg-spare process model" --type=bug --priority=1 --label repo:ethos --description="Successor to ethos-2f2q. That bug's prescribed fix landed: the commit-msg hook now resolves the committing session's own sidecar instead of globbing by mtime, and emits NO trailer when it cannot identify its binding. Correct behaviour. The problem is that resolution now never succeeds under Claude Code's current process model, so the safe fallback is the ONLY path and no commit is ever stamped.

WHERE: internal/resolve/resolve.go, func SessionID (line 144 in the 4.12.0 source I read):

  func SessionID(ss *session.Store) (id, source string) {
      if sid := os.Getenv(\"ETHOS_SESSION\"); sid != \"\" {
          return sid, SessionSourceEnv
      }
      sid, err := ss.ReadCurrentSession(process.FindClaudePID())
      if err != nil { return \"\", \"\" }
      return sid, \"walk\"
  }

Callers: resolveSession -> resolveHardSession -> resolveSessionContext (cmd/ethos/iam.go:45-95), used by iam, mission claim/release, and the bind-on-create path that calls mission.WriteActiveMission (cmd/ethos/mission.go:1946).

THE DEFECT: the session is keyed on a PID that is not stable for the session's lifetime.

MEASURED, xboing-c repo, 2026-09-06:
  session roster participant  = 518779   -> ps: 'claude daemon run', up 11h28m
  process.FindClaudePID()     = 1007618  -> ps: 'claude bg-spare', up 23m
  ETHOS_SESSION               = unset

The roster (782cc6fe-8930-4fff-a35b-7f691da08db9) registered the DAEMON pid at join time. Work then executes in a different process (a background-job spare). ReadCurrentSession(1007618) finds no participant, returns err, SessionID returns \"\", and every caller gets errNoSession.

The PID was observed at three distinct values within one session: 504074 (reported by biff at 07:29), 518779 (recorded in the roster), 1007618 (current at 18:44). Claude Code's daemon-plus-spare model means the PID a subprocess observes is not the PID that registered the roster.

OBSERVED CONSEQUENCES:
1. Every 'mission create' emits: 'binding mission: no session in context -- active-mission sidecar not updated; a subsequent Agent() spawn may still attribute under a previous MISSION_ID'. Nine missions in one session, nine warnings.
2. 'ethos hook commit-trailers' exits 0 printing nothing.
3. Commits made under an OPEN mission with the hook installed and current carry no trailer. Verified: commits a1d7a04 and be9e122 in jmf-pobox/xboing-c, both 'git log -1 --format=%(trailers)' -> empty, made while m-2026-09-06-009 was open, doctor reporting 'Trailer hook currency PASS ... matches this ethos build (sha256:73b3300a)'.
4. Sidecar census: 133 session dirs, exactly 2 contain active-mission, holding m-2026-09-02-006 and m-2026-08-30-014 -- both days stale. No current session ever writes one.
5. ~/.punt-labs/ethos/hook-errors.log had grown to 954 KB of 'ad-hoc Agent spawn (no mission contract)' advisories -- every properly-contracted mission spawn logged as ad-hoc. Same root cause seen from the delegation side.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND METADATA: docs in consuming repos (xboing-c docs/GIT.md) state that a commit without a Mission: trailer means the work skipped the mission process and 'is a defect, not a style choice'. With resolution permanently failing, that rule flags every commit in history. The audit chain git blame -> commit -> trailer -> contract, which is the stated purpose of DES-054, is unreachable.

NOTE THE ESCAPE HATCH ALREADY EXISTS: SessionID checks ETHOS_SESSION first and bypasses the walk entirely. Setting it correctly restores resolution. So a viable immediate mitigation is to have the SessionStart hook export ETHOS_SESSION into the environment ethos subprocesses inherit.

I checked and ruled out a non-PID fallback: ~/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/current exists but is an EMPTY DIRECTORY, not a pointer file. There is currently no stable, non-PID path to the active session.

CAVEAT ON PRECISION: the source I read is the 4.12.0 plugin cache; the installed binary is newer (the warning string 'no session in context' does not appear in 4.12.0 at all, so that text postdates it). Line numbers may have moved. The PID-keyed design and the roster/PID mismatch are measured facts independent of version." --acceptance="A mission created inside a Claude Code session writes ~/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/<id>/active-mission for that session, and a commit made while it is open carries the Mission:/Delegation: trailers. Verified end to end by making a real commit under an open mission and asserting 'git log -1 --format=%(trailers)' is non-empty. Regression covers the case where the process observing FindClaudePID differs from the process that joined the roster." --notes="Found during a full working session in jmf-pobox/xboing-c on 2026-09-06 that ran 9 missions. Related: ethos-2f2q (the predecessor -- its 'emit no trailer rather than a wrong one' guidance is what makes this failure safe rather than corrupting). Worth re-checking whether 2f2q can now be closed: the hook source documents the mtime-globbing fix and now resolves only the committing session." 2>&1 | tail -3

    Audit seal hook          PASS  not enabled here
    Seal hook currency       PASS  no Seal hook section installed

    Seal hook currency       PASS  Seal hook section matches this ethos build (sha256:e7cacc3c)

BE PRECISE ABOUT THE SCOPE OF THIS BUG, because I initially overstated it: the message TEXT does distinguish the two states clearly. What does not distinguish them is the STATUS. Both are PASS. So this is not 'doctor cannot tell'; it is 'doctor knows and does not flag it'.

WHY IT MATTERS: this repo's docs/GIT.md states that a commit lacking a Mission: trailer means the work skipped the mission process and 'is a defect'. The repo had NO trailer hook for an unknown period while doctor reported all-green on that line. The check whose job is to surface exactly this gap reported healthy.

The repo had simply been enabled before the trailer-hook feature existed, and 'ethos enable' -- documented as idempotent, 're-running is the upgrade path' -- had not been re-run. That is precisely the situation a currency check should catch, and the one it stays green for.

SUGGESTED FIX, deliberately narrow: report an absent trailer or seal hook section as WARN rather than PASS when the repo has missions (i.e. .punt-labs/ethos/missions/ is non-empty), with the remedy naming 'ethos enable'.   'A code commit with no mission trailer means the work skipped the mission
   process — that is a defect, not a style choice.'

.claude/rules/delegation.md carries the same framing, and it loads at session start for every agent.

THE RULE HAS NEVER BEEN SATISFIABLE HERE. No commit on master carries a Mission: trailer — checked 'git log master -30' with %(trailers:only), zero hits. So as written the rule marks the entire history defective, which means in practice it is read as noise and ignored. A rule that flags everything discriminates nothing.

WHY IT IS STILL WRONG AFTER THE TOOL IS FIXED. The immediate cause was that no commit-msg hook was installed (resolved 2026-09-06 by 'ethos enable') and that ethos session resolution is broken upstream (ethos-vqwn, P1). But even with both fixed, two classes of commit will legitimately lack a trailer:

  1. every commit predating the hook — the whole existing history
  2. commits genuinely not made under a mission — a typo fix in a README,
     a bead state sync, a revert. delegation.md's own archetype list does
     not require a mission for those, so the rule contradicts it.

So 'missing trailer = the mission process was skipped = defect' is too strong in both directions: it condemns commits that never could have had one, and it offers no way to distinguish 'no mission was needed' from 'a mission was skipped'.

WHAT TO DECIDE — this is a judgement call about the repo's own standard, which is why it is filed rather than fixed:
  a) Scope the rule to commits that touch src/ or tests/ and were made after
     trailers began working, and say so explicitly.
  b) Keep the intent but drop 'defect' — state that a trailer is expected for
     mission-authorized work and that its absence is worth a question, not an
     accusation.
  c) Drop the rule and rely on the mission trail in .punt-labs/ethos/ as the
     audit record, which is where it actually lives.

I lean (b) — the current wording's problem is that it asserts a conclusion ('the work skipped the process') from evidence that does not support it, which is the same class of overstatement this repo spent 2026-09-06 finding in six other places.
